method: Complete three pinned text/source reads, blob/SHA256 verification. Original AST plotting functions executed on pinned bundled JSON with fake chart sink. HTML reviewed as source only, no visual render credit.
findings: Bundled example has nine programs and all numeric records have four fields. Plotter expects five fields including peakmem at2, dupes at3 and sets at4. Original plot_found_results control raises IndexError on bundled example.

Original plot_memory control plots25512 for rmlint from array index2, while separate memory field is147.3617286682129. Thus bundled example and plotting schema cannot support a valid memory comparison together. Units and intended historical schema are not independently established.
unpack tests dictionary length rather than required run keys; average contributes to length. Missing run/average keys can still pass preliminary length check then fail indexing.

Generic plot rounds to three decimals without uncertainty, trial-status or validity checks. Found-results variance calculations are commented out. Graphs cannot supply missing raw-trial correctness or confidence evidence.
Memory uses StackedBar across programs, which aggregates series visually rather than presenting isolated per-program peaks; chart was not rendered here. Timing uses logarithmic scale.
Bundled output records different duplicate counts and swapped-looking dupd/rdfind website metadata; labels/URLs do not establish tool provenance or matched workloads.
Committed HTML table has different program set/counts from bundled example and rounded k values, so it is not established as a rendering of this JSON. No source-to-render provenance inferred.
No benchmark binaries, cold-cache controls or complete equality partitions are supplied by these plotting artifacts. Existing upstream speed claims remain historical.
